title: Linux headless key custody: TPM2-sealed vault key through tpm2-tools, gated on its T26 run (DEC-262)
description: Operator ruling 2026-09-28, relayed by opum-agent (OPAG-675) and binding once opum-doc records it: Ward's committed platforms are macOS, Linux and Windows, matching lore and quest. The first developer preview stays macOS-only. Linux needs a verified, persistent, protected native backend (Secret Service, or another backend that meets spec §6.4). Never a plaintext file or a session-only store. A headless machine without a usable backend fails closed with actionable guidance. Linux is not advertised until its own T26 qualification run passes (spec line 38). Do not build this before WCLI-5 and WCLI-6.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a headless Linux host whose TPM2 is reachable at /dev/tpmrm0 (never /dev/tpm0), a Linux KeyProvider seals the 32-byte vault key itself to the TPM through tpm2-tools. It keeps the sealed public and private blobs and contexts user-private (0600, in Ward's 0700 directory), with no PCR binding. The key unseals after the process and the host restart with nobody present, and cannot be unsealed off-host. The vault format is unchanged (DEC-255 a6). The backend and TPM path are named and measured the way WCLI-5 measured the macOS Keychain.

The vault key reaches tpm2-tools only on a pipe: tpm2_create reads it on stdin and tpm2_unseal writes it on stdout, which Ward reads directly. It never appears in argv, a temp file or the environment. The unseal runs in a salted HMAC session, so the unsealed key never crosses the TPM interface in clear. Tests prove these three properties, and a mocked test does not stand in for the T26 run. If the installed tpm2-tools cannot run the unseal in a salted HMAC session, the slice stops and returns to opum-doc; the libtss2 (bun:ffi) fallback is used only on opum-doc's ruling.

Ward detects the capability by presence, not version. A host without tpm2-tools, without /dev/tpmrm0, or without access to it refuses by name and fails closed in bounded time, naming what to install or which group to join. It never falls back to a plaintext file, a session-only store (including the kernel keyutils keyring) or systemd-creds host-key-only mode. The status and doctor reports say which of three states a host is in: TPM2 absent (unsupported), TPM2 present but not accessible to this user (a named host configuration step), or the blob not user-private. The WCLI-21 ADR states that supported hosts need the tpm2-tools package, and states the threat model: it protects against copying the blob off the host and against other non-root users, not against root or an attacker who boots the same machine.

T26 on a headless Linux host (jetson): a real TPM2 seal-and-unseal integration run and a packaged-binary smoke test pass, including a reboot, and the daemon's effective groups are recorded in the run. Linux is advertised only after that run, and the run is cited where it is advertised. spark stays unsupported by presence until it exposes a TPM2. Desktop-Linux Secret Service is a separate, unadvertised task until it has its own measured T26.

implementationNotes: From WCLI-5: the Keychain adapter fails closed with vault_key_store_unsupported on any platform other than darwin, before constructing an entry. Reason: on Linux, @napi-rs/keyring silently falls back to the kernel keyutils keyring, which does not survive a reboot (per the binding's README). When this task lands, pin the entry explicitly to Secret Service (EntryOptions linux.store) and lift the darwin-only check for that backend alone.

The platform ruling is recorded in opum-doc as ODOC-316 (docs/adr/wards-committed-platform-target-macos-linux-and-windows.md, opum-doc main 900319d), and this repository's docs/adr/0004-committed-platform-target.md states it (WCLI-23).

WCLI-20 review, 2026-09-28: the non-darwin setup lock fallback (O_EXCL file + dead-pid reaping, src/adapters/setup-session.ts) carries a measured check-then-delete race — 12 overlapping holder pairs in 20 rounds, measured by the independent reviewer with process.platform faked. Unreachable today because the key provider refuses non-darwin. Before any platform is qualified, replace the fallback with kernel-arbitrated locking (fcntl F_SETLK, as flock(2) via bun:ffi already does on macOS) or identity-checked compare-and-delete.
Grooming 2026-10-28 (opum-doc approved via team-lead): re-ranked to low, kept.

REWORDED 2026-11-08 under DEC-262 (a9), with (a2) and DEC-255 (a6): the headless backend is a TPM2-sealed vault key through tpm2-tools, replacing the earlier Secret Service KeyProvider framing. Rulings: (a1) build it now, T26 on jetson, spark unsupported by presence; (a2) /dev/tpmrm0 only, access by host configuration, direct to the TPM, blob user-private, doctor reports three states; (a9) Q1 tpm2-tools with the key only on pipes, a salted HMAC session for the unseal, capability detected by presence, libtss2 via bun:ffi only on opum-doc ruling; Q2 no PCR binding; Q3 the vault key itself is sealed, so the vault format is unchanged (DEC-255 a6). WCLI-152 (Linux setup lock) is a prerequisite. Desktop-Linux Secret Service is a separate task. The earlier AC text and the WCLI-5 and WCLI-20 notes above it are history.

SLICE 2 DESIGN NOTE 2026-11-08, from the #294 review (finding 7): the setup lock lives on an open file description. A child spawned while it is held (for example tpm2-tools run by a TPM provider) shares that description if the fd lacks close-on-exec, and keeps the lock held after the parent exits. That costs liveness, not safety: it never lets two processes hold the lock. Slice 2 must confirm that Bun openSync sets O_CLOEXEC, or that its spawns do not pass inherited fds, and test it. Also carried into slice 2 (opum-doc, DEC-262 a9): a fresh salted session for every unseal with tpm2_sessionconfig decrypt/encrypt reported as a pass/fail check, and Ward sets and verifies 0600 itself on every blob and context file it writes.

SLICE 2 SPLIT, 2026-11-08 (review finding 10 on opum-ai/ward-cli#301, round 1). Slice 2 lands as 2a then 2b, one PR each, each with its own Opus review. 2a (#301): src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts presence detection (order: TPM2 device absent, then tools absent, then device not openable), bounded and output-capped tool spawning in a minimal environment (PATH and TPM2TOOLS_TCTI only), Ward-owned 0700/0600 set-and-verify, and the #294 finding-7 lock-inheritance test; fake tpm2_* executables under test/fixtures/fake-tpm2. 2b OWES: seal (tpm2_createprimary, tpm2_create reading the key on stdin) and unseal (tpm2_load, then a FRESH salted HMAC session per unseal, never a reused context, with tpm2_sessionconfig reporting decrypt/encrypt as a pass/fail check in the tests and in T26; off is the AC2 stop), the key never in argv, a temp file or the environment, and the session context file asserted 0600 before tpm2_unseal reads it. 2b does not start piping a real key until opum-doc rules on which binary the key reaches (resolveTool trusts the first executable regular file on any absolute PATH entry; review finding 3). Round-1 findings 1, 2, 4-9 and 10 were taken in the 2a fix; finding 3 is routed to opum-doc. Measured under finding 2c: Bun.spawn does not pass a descriptor lacking close-on-exec (a dup(2) of the flocked fd is not inherited by a plain spawn on macOS; the Linux Check job is the other half), so what keeps the setup lock out of a spawned tool is Bun.spawn, not openSync O_CLOEXEC; setup-session.ts needs no change.

SLICE 2a REVIEW, round 2, 2026-11-08, VERBATIM from the Opus reviewer ward-cli-review-301b (claude-opus-5-5, verify MATCH), copied here because the opum-agent scratchpad does not persist. opum-ai/ward-cli#301 landed as 298495f13cc861a42a33b6c658ee11c5725b5ffe on dev. Round-2 review of opum-ai/ward-cli#301 (WCLI-21 slice 2a): APPROVE, provided Check is green at the full head SHA; ten non-blocking findings.
VERDICT: APPROVE
HEAD: 0070edcc88a1e622dfac4da52dd1850a0e440b79
Reviewer: read-only unit (DEC-183 Stage 1), model claude-opus-5-5, worktree ward-cli-review-301b. I read the round-1 verdict, the full r2 diff, the r1→r2 delta, and WCLI-21.json at HEAD. I also read isPrivateEntry, setup-session.ts (it locks with flock, so the flock-based controls are like for like), immediate-timers.ts, ci.yml and the CLI's exitExplicitly path.
The approval depends on the Check job being green at the full 0070edcc SHA. I can't read CI; you can. The "measured" mechanism test and the Linux half of the WCLI-21 note both rest on that run.

Round-1 findings
- 1: Resolved in code, partly resolved in the test.
  - defaultOpenCheck now opens and closes the device (src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts:123-125: closeSync(openSync(device, O_RDWR))). EACCES/EPERM map to tpm_not_accessible and any other errno to tpm_unusable (:174-181).
  - The default-path test goes red if the check becomes a no-op. It stays green if the check is reverted to accessSync(R_OK|W_OK), because a mode-denied device fails access(2) and open(2) alike. See new finding 1. The production code is correct now, so this does not block.
- 2(a): Resolved. The control passes the flocked fd as stdio slot 3 (test/tpm2-tools.test.ts:590-596). If Bun ignored that slot, the acquire would succeed and the control would go red, so it can fail.
- 2(b): Resolved as asked, but the second assertion is inert.
  - expect(child.exitCode).toBeNull() at :636 now follows the re-acquire. There is still no await between the spawn and the assertion, though, and I expect Bun to update exitCode only on an event-loop turn (unverified).
  - The scenario round 1 raised is implausible here anyway. Bun.spawn returns after exec, so the child's descriptors are already final when the re-acquire runs. The hang fixture blocks on a stdin pipe the test never closes, so the child cannot die in that window.
  - To make the assertion real: before asserting, race child.exited against Bun.sleep(50) and expect the sleep to win.
- 2(c): Resolved. The "measured" test dups the flocked fd, so close-on-exec is clear, spawns /bin/sleep, and re-acquires (:599-622). It goes red if Bun passes a descriptor that lacks close-on-exec. The mechanism is recorded in a test comment and in the WCLI-21 note. The note says it was measured on macOS and that the Linux half is the CI run.
- 4: Resolved for stdout.
  - readCapped caps each stream at 4096 bytes and cancels the reader. The flood test (:380) goes red if the cap is removed.
  - The stderr cap has no test, so removing it alone stays green.
- 5: Resolved.
  - runTool races the work against a timer that sends SIGKILL and rejects at once. work.catch and timeout.catch prevent unhandled rejections, and Promise.race prevents double resolution.
  - The grandchild test (:428) goes red if runTool waits for EOF: that wait is 30 s, past bun's 5 s test timeout.
  - The stdin write and end are wrapped, and a test sends an unread 4 MiB stdin.
  - Residuals are new findings 4, 5 and 9.
- 6: Partly resolved.
  - adoptToolFile now uses one fd opened O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW, then fstat, fchmod and fstat (:326-346). The fd is closed in a finally, and nothing leaks on the error paths.
  - The symlink test goes red if O_NOFOLLOW is dropped: the target's 0644 would become 0600, and the adopt would succeed.
  - Still open: nothing requires the path's parent to be a verified 0700 directory, and O_NOFOLLOW covers only the last path component. There is a new defect too, new finding 2.
- 7: Resolved. accessRemedy derives the group from the device gid, and a mode without group rw says "host configuration" (:142-149). The test with an injected group name goes red if "tss" is hardcoded again. Residual: new finding 3.
- 8: Resolved. directory_unusable covers mkdir failures and tpm_unusable covers any other open errno, and both are tested (ENOENT, and an injected EROFS).
- 9: Partly resolved. The allow-list plus the banned-call scan, with its control, is a real improvement. Gaps remain: new finding 6.
- 10: Resolved. The "SLICE 2 SPLIT" note on WCLI-21 records 2a, what 2b owes (a fresh salted session per unseal, sessionconfig decrypt/encrypt as a pass/fail check, the session context asserted 0600) and the hold for finding 3.
- 3: Out of scope (DEC-262 (a10), slice 2b). The symlinked multicall test is sound. The fixture writes its record under ${0##*/}, so the test goes red under lstatSync (tools_absent) and also goes red if the spawn resolves the symlink, because the record would land under "tpm2".

New findings (all non-blocking)
1. test/tpm2-tools.test.ts:246-270. The default-path test can't tell open(2) from access(2).
   - Scenario: someone "simplifies" defaultOpenCheck back to accessSync, and the suite stays green. That is round-1 finding 1's original defect.
   - The regex /^tpm_(not_accessible|unusable)$/ at :263 also hides an EACCES→tpm_unusable mapping regression on the default path.
   - Fix: expect defaultOpenCheck(<a temp directory>) to throw EISDIR. access(R_OK|W_OK) passes on that directory and open(O_RDWR) refuses it. Also tighten :263 to tpm_not_accessible, because a mode-denied device is always refused with EACCES.
2. src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts:329. adoptToolFile opens before it checks the file type, and the open has no O_NONBLOCK.
   - Scenario: a FIFO at the path makes openSync(O_RDONLY) block until a writer appears, so the process hangs with no bound, against AC2's "bounded time".
   - A device node at the path gets opened, with that device's open side effects, before !isFile() refuses it.
   - Only this user can plant one inside Ward's 0700 directory, but nothing requires that directory.
   - Fix: add O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY to the open (the fstat still refuses a non-regular file), or lstat and refuse a non-regular file before opening. Add a test that a FIFO is refused promptly.
3. src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts:142-149. The remedy is wrong in exactly the cases finding 1 was about.
   - Scenario A: AppArmor refuses the open of a 0660 root:tss device for a user already in tss. The refusal says "join the tss group", but the user is in it, and the fix is the profile.
   - Scenario B: the user was added to tss after this session started, so /etc/group lists them and process.getgroups() doesn't. The step is a new login. AC3 records the daemon's effective groups for this reason.
   - Fix: compare the device's gid and mode with process.getgroups(). If DAC already grants access, say a security policy refused it and a host configuration change is needed. If the group lists the user but the process lacks it, say to start a new login session.
4. src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts:241-285. A timed-out runTool can keep the CLI alive, and the grandchild is never killed.
   - After a timeout, the work's pipe reads stay pending, along with child.exited for a child stuck in the driver. src/cli/ward.ts:17 exits explicitly only when a provider reports abandonedCall (the WCLI-5 pattern). runTool gives slice 3 no such signal.
   - Scenario: `ward doctor` returns tool_timeout, then the process hangs until a grandchild closes the pipe or the child leaves D-state.
   - Only the direct child is killed; a grandchild is orphaned.
   - Fix (slice 3 at the latest): treat tool_timeout as an abandoned call so the CLI exits explicitly, or cancel the readers and child.unref() on timeout. If Bun supports it, spawn the tool in its own process group and kill the group.
5. test/tpm2-tools.test.ts:428-442. The grandchild test is a flake risk on the required Check.
   - The fake has to cold-start bun and read stdin to EOF before it spawns the grandchild and writes grandchild.pid. If that takes longer than the 300 ms bound on a contended runner (WCLI-53 measured a 150 ms bound reading 474 ms), the child is killed first.
   - Then readFileSync(grandchild.pid) throws ENOENT, the test goes red, and that run never exercised the grandchild case.
   - The grandchild is also left running if an assertion throws before process.kill.
   - Fix: a timeout of about 2–3 s, the grandchild's sleep raised to about 60 s, a ceiling well under that sleep, and the kill in a finally.
6. test/tpm2-tools.test.ts:290-316. The fallback checker has holes.
   - (a) "./sqlite-vault-store.ts" is an allowed module with no name check. That module is a vault store, so `import { <any writer> } from "./sqlite-vault-store.ts"` passes as "no fallback". Restrict it to isPrivateEntry, the same way node:fs is name-checked.
   - (b) The import regex only matches the `import { … } from "…"` form. `import * as fs from "node:fs"` followed by fs.copyFileSync(...), a dynamic import(), or require() never reaches the allow-list.
   - (c) The banned-call scan misses Bun.file(p).writer(), and the keyutils CLI (`keyctl`) through Bun.spawn.
   - Fix: flag any import form that isn't `{…}`, name-check every allowed module, and add Bun.file, keyctl and import(/require( to the scan. Extend the control to cover each.
7. test/tpm2-tools.test.ts:225. The /dev sweep opens every candidate character device O_RDWR.
   - DAC refuses these for a non-root user, and root skips the test. But the filter checks mode bits only and ignores POSIX ACLs and capabilities.
   - Worst case: on a node an ACL grants, or for a non-root process holding CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, the open succeeds. If that node is /dev/watchdog, the open arms the hardware timer, and with nowayout, closing it without the magic byte reboots the host. A tty opened without O_NOCTTY can also become the controlling terminal, or block waiting for carrier.
   - Fix: use an explicit inert candidate list (/dev/mem, /dev/port, /dev/kmsg) instead of readdirSync, and keep failing on zero candidates on Linux.
8. src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts:28. The 4096-byte cap is sized for tpm2_unseal, and the comment says so for every tool.
   - tpm2_createprimary and tpm2_create print the public area as YAML; an RSA2048 modulus alone is 512 hex characters. Verbose TSS2 error logging on stderr can also pass the cap, so a real failure would be reported as tool_output_too_large rather than tool_failed.
   - Owed to 2b: pass -Q where it applies, or measure the output on jetson, and consider truncating stderr rather than refusing it, since stderr is only diagnostic.
9. src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts:258-263 (optional). runTool awaits stdin.end() before it starts either reader.
   - A tool that fills its stdout pipe before reading stdin deadlocks until the timer fires, and is reported as tool_timeout instead of tool_output_too_large.
   - It's harmless for a 32-byte key. Fix: start both readCapped calls before writing stdin.
10. src/adapters/tpm2-tools.ts:202 (optional). spawnTool can throw a raw error.
    - If a tool is removed between detection and spawn, Bun.spawn throws synchronously. The error escapes as a raw Error, not a Tpm2Error, so slice 3's reason mapping never sees it.
    - Fix: wrap the spawn and map the error to tool_failed or tools_absent.

Secrets: nothing secret reaches logs, errors, argv or the environment. Tpm2Error details carry only tool names, errno codes and group names. The environment is exactly PATH plus TPM2TOOLS_TCTI. A failed or over-cap run discards stdout. Bytes travel only on stdin. The fixtures use synthetic values only.
Device side effects in production: an open and close of /dev/tpmrm0 only allocates and frees a resource-manager space, and sends no TPM command. defaultOpenCheck cannot leak an fd: a failed open gives no fd, and close releases the fd even when it reports an error.

Acceptance criteria (WCLI-21; this slice claims none fully met)

  - New findings 2, 3, 4 and 6 bear on this slice's parts.
- AC3: Not in this slice.
- Slice-2 design note: the lock-inheritance test is met, with the mechanism measured and recorded. "Ward sets and verifies 0600" is met for the primitive. The salted session is deferred to 2b and recorded on WCLI-21.

  - whether Bun.spawn honours a numeric fd in stdio slot 3 (the 2(a) control);
  - whether Bun.spawn on Linux leaves a descriptor that lacks close-on-exec out of the child (2(c));

SLICE 3 MAPPING OWES, from the #306 round 2 APPROVE: when Tpm2Reason values are mapped to contract error codes and doctor states, platform_unsupported (a runtime lacking O_NOFOLLOW, O_NONBLOCK or O_NOCTTY, raised by safeOpenFlags) must be mapped too; nothing forces it until the mapping exists. Slice 2b part 1 (the DEC-262 (a10)/(a11) tool-trust walk) landed as opum-ai/ward-cli#308, squash c1a5624 on dev, after two Opus review rounds (APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS, both met at 2a1388a). Tpm2Host carries no trust policy: detectTpm2 and assertToolTrusted always read real lstat owner and mode, trusted uids root plus the invoking user, walk to /; narrowing exists only as detectTpm2ForTest and walkToolTrustForTest, with a test that fails if src/ names them elsewhere. Production detectTpm2 is tested both ways under a clean and a 0777 checkout directory. Residual gaps (shebang interpreter, shared libraries, full child PATH) filed as a new task. Next: slice 2b part 2 (seal/unseal), only on the leader brief; the walk is reviewed, so a real key may now be piped in that slice, with its own floor and Opus review.

Owed to the slice 3 ADR (from the #313 review, finding 6): record the DEC-262 (a12) rule 3 residual, that an ELF RUNPATH pointing at a directory another user can write is a packaging defect outside AC2 and that Ward does not parse ELF.

Residuals from the #313 (WCLI-164) Opus review, for the slice 3 ADR beside the RUNPATH one; out of DEC-262 (a14) scope as ruled, not defects in #313, and each needs a trusted owner to write the shebang (the packaging-defect class of an ELF RUNPATH). (1) Spotting env by name misses a hardlink or copy of env under another name, and a multicall alias whose written and final names are both something else. (2) Other single-argument wrappers (nice, nohup, timeout, stdbuf, or a shebang of /bin/sh /abs/script) can run an unwalked absolute path through the one shebang argument. NON-BLOCKING NITS to fold into the 2b part 2 PR: the wrapped interpreter walk error in tpm2-tools.ts should read toolPath: its shebang interpreter: detail (no repeated interpreter); an unreadable interpreter should say it is the interpreter (label toolPath: its shebang interpreter); fix the comment implying CR is refused later than the printable-ASCII check (that check refuses it first); the env alias test should assert basename(realpathSync of /usr/bin/env) is env as a precondition, or use a stand-in named env in the tree; delete the dead / early return in walkToolTrust, the presence.path field no longer used for spawning, and walk /usr/bin and /bin once per detection, not once per tool.

Owed to the slice 3 ADR (from the #316 seal review). (1) The pinned primary template (tpm2_createprimary -C o -g sha256 -G ecc256:aes128cfb -a restricted|decrypt|fixedtpm|fixedparent|sensitivedataorigin|userwithauth|noda) and the sealed-object attributes (fixedtpm|fixedparent|noda|userwithauth, sha256, no PCR policy) are part of the on-disk contract, with the reasons; the blob loads only under the primary it was created under, and a changed default would orphan it. (2) noda exempts the objects from dictionary-attack lockout and pairs with an EMPTY userauth: revisit it if an authValue is ever added. (3) tpm2_clear or an owner-hierarchy password makes the blob permanently unloadable: Ward needs a named state and a recovery story for each. (4) Same-uid access: with empty userauth the 0600 mode is the only barrier and any process under this uid can load and unseal; this is already accepted by ADR 0001 (Consequences) under the ADR 0002 threat model, and the ADR states it for the TPM backend citing both. (5) For 2b part 2b (unseal): never surface tpm2_unseal stderr; keep TSS2_LOG out of the built environment; MEASURE FIRST on jetson whether a session saved by tpm2_startauthsession survives into a SEPARATE tpm2_unseal process under /dev/tpmrm0 (the resource manager flushes a connection sessions on close), since it bears on the AC1 stop condition; load the sealed blob under the SAME primary context used as the salt key, then assert tpm2_sessionconfig reports encrypt and decrypt on that session. (6) The fake tool writes a 0660 file for -c on every tool; for unseal, startauthsession and load, -c/-S is an input: give the fake a per-tool output-flag map and fail when a named input is missing (finding 10, deferred to the unseal PR).
